paragraphs: A model can struggle when an image's colors differ from those seen during training. Color-equivariant architectures address this by making their internal representations transform predictably when colors change. This paper identifies a geometric problem in earlier designs: saturation and luminance occupy bounded intervals, but those designs treat changes in them as translations along an unbounded line.

The proposed architecture instead lifts each interval onto a circle using a double-cover construction. This gives the network a space in which it can build equivariant representations without the interval-to-line approximation. The central contribution is therefore a change in how color transformations are represented, resolving the artifacts attributed to the earlier geometry.

The authors report improved interpretability, generalization, and predictive performance compared with conventional and color-equivariant baselines on fine-grained classification and medical imaging tasks. They also show that the lifting construction can extend to geometric transformations such as scale. These findings connect the practical gains to a representation that respects the structure of the transformed quantities.
icml-2026-a-hypertoroidal-covering-for-p.tldr: A circle-based representation of bounded color quantities removes approximation artifacts and improves color-equivariant image models.

paragraphs: Distributed training must balance work performed locally against communication between agents, especially when their data distributions differ. This paper studies that tradeoff for stochastic, strongly convex optimization. It develops a method that combines accelerated updates to dual variables with several stochastic gradient descent steps on the primal variables in a Lagrangian formulation.

The local gradient steps require no communication between agents. To analyze their effect, the authors view the resulting partial gradient with respect to the dual variables as an approximate gradient of the dual objective. This connects incomplete local optimization to an inexact accelerated gradient framework, allowing the analysis to account for the errors introduced by local updates.

The method is proved to converge for any number of local updates. It reaches optimal communication complexity when enough local computation is available, so that stronger conclusion is explicitly conditional. The same analytical framework also yields an algorithm with optimal reproducibility guarantees under biased gradient estimates, extending its relevance beyond the communication tradeoff.
icml-2026-accelerated-dual-method-for-di.tldr: An inexact-gradient analysis supports accelerated distributed optimization with local updates and conditionally optimal communication complexity.

paragraphs: Brain prediction systems often begin by constructing a fixed network from correlation coefficients, then train a sophisticated predictor on that network. This paper argues that the construction step can discard useful information before learning begins. Improving the downstream graph model may therefore leave a bottleneck in the representation itself unresolved.

The authors formulate Brain Representation learning, or BRep, in which the brain network becomes a learnable graph representation. Their approach extends familiar linear and nonlinear correlations into higher-order, parameterized forms that can be learned. More of the modeling capacity consequently moves into the representation, allowing the downstream predictor to remain simple while still producing accurate predictions.

The theoretical result establishes universal approximation for U/V-statistics, giving the representation a specific mathematical expressivity guarantee. Evaluations report superior performance, efficiency, and interpretability. Together, these results support learning how the brain network is formed as an important part of the prediction problem, rather than concentrating the modeling effort entirely on a network that has already been fixed.
icml-2026-brain-networks-should-be-learn.tldr: BRep learns the brain network itself, producing expressive representations that support simple, accurate downstream predictors.

paragraphs: A vision-language model may understand a task yet apply the wrong decision criterion. This paper studies situations where the overall task stays fixed but the criterion determining the correct answer changes. Its Criterion-Conditional In-Context Learning setting asks models to infer that criterion from contextual examples and adapt their predictions without parameter updates.

The authors introduce two complementary measures, Criterion Invariance and Criterion Sensitivity, to evaluate robustness and adaptation under criterion changes. Their CC-Bench benchmark uses a two-level data hierarchy so that different answers can legitimately be correct under different active criteria. This makes criterion adaptation an explicit evaluation target instead of assuming that understanding the general task is sufficient.

Experiments find that most evaluated models retain rigid decision boundaries and struggle to follow the contextual criterion. A simple training strategy involving multiple criteria substantially reduces this bias and improves sensitivity. Under the reported evaluation, it also enables models at the 7B scale to outperform proprietary models without reducing general multimodal performance.
icml-2026-criterion-conditional-in-conte.tldr: CC-Bench tests whether vision-language models adapt to changing decision criteria, revealing rigidity that multi-criterion training can reduce.

paragraphs: This paper studies learners connected through a network that must collectively respond to a sequence of losses. Each learner sees local information and compressed messages from its neighbors. The challenge is to keep cumulative regret low while communication loses information, particularly when compression quality is poor or agreement across the network is difficult.

The proposed algorithm organizes updates through two levels of blocks. An online gossip strategy and an error compensation mechanism work together to improve agreement among learners. Its regret bounds have substantially milder dependence on compression quality than previous bounds and replace their undesirable super-linear dependence on the number of learners with a linear factor, up to logarithmic terms.

The analysis covers both convex and strongly convex losses, with different guarantees for the two settings. New lower bounds justify optimality with respect to compression quality and the time horizon, rather than every problem parameter. The authors also extend the approach to bandit feedback using classical gradient estimators, improving existing regret bounds when direct gradient information is unavailable.
icml-2026-decentralized-online-convex-op.tldr: A blocking, gossip, and error-compensation scheme improves regret guarantees for decentralized learning with compressed communication.

paragraphs: Training-free image editing commonly turns an image into a noisy representation, then follows separate forward paths to reconstruct and edit it. This paper identifies a source of reconstruction drift: existing methods approximate the reconstruction path using noisy representations associated with mismatched timesteps. Those errors accumulate and reduce fidelity to the original image.

DirectEdit addresses this by directly aligning the forward paths within a flow transformer. The authors describe this alignment as eliminating the inherent reconstruction error without adding neural function evaluations. Accurate reconstruction also supports reliable sharing of features between the reconstruction and editing processes, connecting inversion accuracy to the editing method itself.

A preservation mechanism combines attention feature injection with mask-guided noise blending across multiple branches. Its purpose is to retain desired image content while still allowing the requested edit. Experiments across diverse scenarios report efficient, accurate editing and better performance than state-of-the-art methods. The contribution joins step-level alignment with explicit preservation controls, addressing both reconstruction fidelity and editability.
icml-2026-directedit-step-level-accurate.tldr: DirectEdit aligns forward editing paths to eliminate inherent reconstruction error without extra neural function evaluations.

paragraphs: Removing undesirable knowledge and refusing to use it solve related but different problems. The paper argues that deletion methods can suppress particular token sequences without fully removing the underlying knowledge, while refusal methods leave that knowledge intact and potentially available again. It proposes Distinguishable Deletion to combine erasure with a coherent response to inputs concerning erased content.

The approach constrains response distributions through latent representations rather than targeting specific output tokens. It also separates knowledge selected for removal from knowledge that should remain. An energy index measures knowledge presence and this separation, providing a shared quantity for managing both the training-time deletion process and inference-time refusal.

The implementation, Energy-based Unlearning Alignment, applies energy boundaries during training and uses energy to guide refusal afterward. Mathematical and empirical analyses support the index's accuracy and efficiency, while experiments report substantial improvements over previous methods. The stated results support coordinating deletion and refusal through the same representation-level signal, with retained knowledge explicitly distinguished from content being unlearned.
icml-2026-distinguishable-deletion-unify.tldr: Distinguishable Deletion uses representation-level energy boundaries to coordinate knowledge removal and refusal in language models.

paragraphs: A model that generates images while reasoning might appear to use those images as evidence, even if its answers mostly depend on text. This paper asks whether unified foundation models actually connect their generated visual content to later decisions. Evaluating image generation and understanding separately cannot establish that functional connection.

The authors introduce UFO, a benchmark for compositional reasoning with generated image and text cues. It covers state determination, state reconstruction, and state augmentation, ordered by progressively smaller changes to the underlying world state. These regimes provide a way to examine evidence use across different kinds of state-transition reasoning within the same evaluation framework.

The analysis reveals a substantial gap between modalities: models often predict accurately even when their generated images have little influence on the decision. The authors interpret this as weakened coupling between visual evidence and reasoning, alongside reliance on textual shortcuts. The finding makes answer accuracy alone an incomplete indicator of whether a model grounds its reasoning in both modalities.
icml-2026-do-vision-and-text-cues-exhibi.tldr: UFO finds that accurate multimodal answers can coexist with weak use of generated visual evidence.

paragraphs: Offline preference training relies on an already collected dataset, making corrupted preference labels a potential vulnerability. This paper studies targeted label flips specifically for log-linear Direct Preference Optimization. Its starting observation is that reversing one preference label changes the training gradient by an amount that does not depend on the model parameters.

That property lets the authors express poisoning as a structured problem of selecting a sparse set of binary choices. They develop a lattice-based method, BAL-A, and a matching-pursuit method, BMP-A. For the lattice approach, they give sufficient conditions for enforcing binary coefficients and recovering the minimum-flip objective. These are conditional guarantees rather than a claim that recovery always succeeds.

For BMP-A, the analysis connects recovery to dictionary coherence and provides certificates showing when attacks are impossible within a specified flip budget. Experiments on synthetic dictionaries and the Stanford Human Preferences dataset support the theory. The results highlight the geometry of the available gradient shifts as a determinant of attack success and robustness.
icml-2026-efficient-preference-poisoning.tldr: For log-linear DPO, preference-label poisoning becomes a structured binary selection problem with conditional recovery and robustness guarantees.

paragraphs: A reward model can assign high scores for superficial attributes that do not reflect the behavior people actually prefer. Optimizing against such a model can produce reward hacking: the score improves without a corresponding improvement in behavior. This paper addresses that problem by separating the contextual representation used to predict rewards into two components.

One component is intended to contain causal factors sufficient for reward prediction. The other captures reward-irrelevant attributes, including length or sycophantic bias. The reward prediction head can access only the causal component. An additional adversarial head tries to predict reward from the non-causal component, while gradient reversal discourages that component from retaining reward-relevant information.

Experiments on mathematical and dialogue tasks report more robust reward models and consistent improvements in downstream RLHF over state-of-the-art baselines. Analyses focused on length and sycophancy also support reduced reward hacking. These findings support controlling which parts of a learned representation can influence reward predictions as a way to improve the behavior produced by subsequent optimization.
icml-2026-factored-causal-representation.tldr: Separating reward-relevant and irrelevant representations improves reward robustness and reduces observed reward hacking in RLHF.

paragraphs: Reasoning models often spend substantial computation generating long answers from short prompts. Sparse attention can reduce that cost, but repeatedly choosing the wrong tokens can damage reasoning over a long generation. LessIsMore is a training-free attention method designed around the observation that important reasoning tokens are largely shared across heads and remain stable across decoding steps.

The method makes attention heads use a unified token selection and retains recent tokens through a stable recency window. This produces a consistent set of tokens that can also be reused across layers. The approach uses the observed shared structure of token importance to reduce repeated selection disagreements while preserving access to recent context.

Across multiple model families and reasoning benchmarks, the authors report matching or improving accuracy while attending to substantially fewer tokens. Kernel optimizations deliver up to 1.6 times faster end-to-end decoding and up to 1.72 times faster sparse attention computation. Those figures are reported maxima. Additional long-context results support applicability beyond the main long-horizon reasoning evaluations.
icml-2026-less-is-more-fast-and-accurate.tldr: LessIsMore shares sparse token selections across attention heads, preserving reasoning accuracy while achieving up to 1.6× faster decoding.

paragraphs: Converting a natural-language request into SQL requires precise logic and correct use of a database schema. MARS-SQL makes the workflow for this task trainable by dividing it among three roles: grounding the request in the schema, generating queries, and validating solutions. Its contribution centers on learning how those activities support an interactive solution process.

The generation agent uses a multi-turn reinforcement learning policy within a reasoning-and-action loop. It executes intermediate SQL against a live database and uses execution feedback to refine its strategy. A separate validation mechanism ranks interaction trajectories through next-token prediction probabilities, treating selection of a solution as a generative modeling task.

The evaluations support combining interactive learning with trajectory ranking. MARS-SQL reports execution accuracy of 77.84% on the BIRD development dataset and 89.75% on the Spider test dataset, along with strong transfer to out-of-domain benchmarks. These results connect its reported state-of-the-art performance to a workflow that learns from database interaction and evaluates the resulting solution trajectories.
icml-2026-mars-sql-a-multi-agent-reinfor.tldr: MARS-SQL trains specialized agents to generate SQL through database feedback and rank their solution trajectories.

paragraphs: Clustering data with several views becomes difficult when many views are missing and some are observed much more often than others. Few jointly observed examples make relationships between views unreliable. MAGIC addresses this by first learning calibrated cluster assignments, then using those assignments to guide conservative completion of missing representations.

The framework builds several related representation and prediction paths from lightly augmented latent codes. Masked contrastive consensus and prediction consistency encourage those paths to agree. Their posterior predictions are combined into soft cluster assignments for each view, aiming to reduce overconfidence and prevent frequently available views from dominating the learned clustering.

MAGIC then transfers semantic information in label space using similarity and confidence gates. A prototype fallback completes representations while preserving geometry. Experiments on four benchmarks with different missing-data ratios show consistent improvements over earlier incomplete multi-view clustering methods. Ablations support both the consensus-learning component and confidence-gated imputation, linking the gains to how cluster meaning is established before missing information is filled in.
icml-2026-masked-multi-path-contrast-wit.tldr: MAGIC learns calibrated cluster assignments before confidence-gated completion, improving clustering when views are missing or unevenly available.

paragraphs: A pretrained model that learns tasks sequentially can overwrite earlier knowledge, especially when historical training data is unavailable. This paper links that interference to two factors: sharp regions of the loss landscape and dominant singular-value directions during model merging. SAIM addresses both the way each task is learned and the way task knowledge is combined.

During fine-tuning, a sharpness-aware block coordinate descent optimizer seeks flatter minima and selectively updates parameters most sensitive to the task. During merging, an adaptive isotropic algorithm balances the singular-value spectrum across tasks. This aims to keep one task direction from dominating the combined representation and improve alignment between task subspaces.

Experiments on vision and language benchmarks report accuracy improvements of 5–10% over existing methods, together with robust performance as the task count grows. The results support treating fine-tuning and merging as connected sources of forgetting. SAIM's two components address parameter interference during learning and imbalanced representation of task knowledge during combination.
icml-2026-merge-to-remember-sharpness-aw.tldr: SAIM combines sharpness-aware fine-tuning with balanced model merging to reduce forgetting across sequential tasks.

paragraphs: Prompt tuning adapts a pretrained vision-language model by learning a small set of prompt vectors. With limited supervision, however, those prompts can move the resulting representations away from the pretrained geometry in directions that transfer poorly. This paper presents that drift as a mechanism for overfitting and introduces ManiPT to constrain it.

ManiPT applies cosine consistency constraints to both image and text representations, keeping learned features within the geometric neighborhood established during pretraining. It also introduces a structural preference for incremental corrections. Together, these mechanisms guide adaptation toward transferable directions and reduce reliance on shortcuts that fit the limited training data.

The theoretical analysis supports reduced overfitting tendencies under limited data. Experiments cover unseen-class generalization, few-shot classification, cross-dataset transfer, and domain generalization, with higher average performance than baseline methods across these settings. The findings connect transfer quality to preservation of pretrained representation geometry and provide a concrete account of why otherwise parameter-efficient prompt tuning can still overfit.
icml-2026-prompt-tuning-for-clip-on-the-.tldr: ManiPT constrains prompt tuning near CLIP's pretrained representation geometry to reduce overfitting and improve transfer.

paragraphs: Language models can propose rules in ordinary language, avoiding the need to define every possible predicate beforehand. But a collection of plausible rules still needs a reliable way to combine their effects. RLIE addresses the interactions among rules by pairing language-model rule discovery with a probabilistic model that learns their relative importance.

The framework first generates and filters candidate rules. Logistic regression then learns sparse, calibrated weights for selecting and combining them globally. An iterative refinement stage revisits the rules using difficult examples identified through errors. Finally, the authors compare different inference approaches to evaluate how the learned rules work as a complete reasoning system.

Across multiple real-world datasets and model backbones, the weighted rules deliver better accuracy and stability. Simply inserting rules into prompts produces mixed results and often hurts performance. The authors interpret this as evidence that language models are effective semantic rule discoverers but less reliable probabilistic aggregators, supporting a division of responsibilities between language-based discovery and explicit statistical combination.
icml-2026-rlie-rule-generation-with-logi.tldr: RLIE combines language-model rule discovery with learned probabilistic weights, improving accuracy and stability over less controlled rule use.

paragraphs: Preference optimization can align diffusion-generated images and videos with human choices, but its training updates can be unstable. This paper examines both high gradient variance across timesteps and mismatch between the optimization data and the current model distribution. Its trajectory analysis identifies early timesteps with low importance weights as the main source of instability.

SIPO uses a gradient modification called DPO-C&M to clip updates and mask uninformative timesteps. It then applies timestep-aware importance reweighting to correct off-policy bias and emphasize informative updates. The two mechanisms address different aspects of alignment: how noisy or sensitive an update is, and how well its training data reflects the policy being optimized.

Experiments include SD1.5 and SDXL for images, plus CogVideoX and Wan models for video. With careful parameter adjustments, the authors report consistently more stable training and better performance than existing alignment methods. The findings support treating timestep contributions explicitly during preference optimization, with the reported improvements tied to the tuned experimental configurations.
icml-2026-sipo-stabilized-and-improved-p.tldr: SIPO stabilizes diffusion preference training through timestep clipping, masking, and importance reweighting.

paragraphs: Symmetric multimodal retrieval searches between items containing both images and text, with either side able to serve as the query. Existing universal retrieval methods struggle because their labeled training datasets impose asymmetric roles. SOLAR addresses this using a two-stage self-supervised framework trained from readily available, unlabeled image-text pairs.

The first stage learns a mask representing the semantic intersection between an image and its text. It aligns shared meaning while preserving information that appears in only one modality. The second stage uses that mask to hide different portions of images or text, constructing positive examples and difficult negatives for learning multimodal embeddings.

The authors also introduce a benchmark with human-verified positive and hard-negative pairs. Against ten state-of-the-art methods, SOLAR exceeds the strongest supervised vision-language model by 7.08 points on that benchmark, while using over 50 times fewer parameters and embeddings five times smaller. These results support learning from both shared and differing image-text content for this symmetric retrieval setting.
icml-2026-solar-self-supervised-joint-le.tldr: SOLAR learns symmetric multimodal retrieval from unlabeled image-text pairs by modeling both shared and modality-specific meaning.

paragraphs: Speech understanding and general audio understanding often rely on separately optimized representations. SPEAR aims to bring those capabilities into one self-supervised model by learning from two complementary teachers: one focused on speech and another focused on general audio. The goal is a representation useful across both domains.

The framework converts continuous teacher representations into fine-grained discrete tokens using multiple vector-quantization codebooks. These tokens capture semantic and acoustic information. Given masked input, the student jointly predicts the different teacher tokens using an asymmetric pretraining loss. A token-mixing mechanism further improves robustness in complex sound scenes, helping integrate the heterogeneous learning signals.

The authors report consistent improvements over existing unified speech-and-audio models. SPEAR achieves a new state of the art on SUPERB and surpasses WavLM Large on 12 of its 15 tasks, while remaining competitive on HEAR. The combination of results supports the proposed unified representation, with the strongest stated benchmark outcome in speech and competitive performance in broader audio evaluation.
icml-2026-spear-a-unified-ssl-framework-.tldr: SPEAR distills speech and general-audio teachers into one model, achieving leading SUPERB results and competitive HEAR performance.

paragraphs: An audio scene can contain both benign and harmful intentions, while its accompanying text gives little indication of the risk. SACRED-Bench evaluates how multimodal language models handle that combination. It examines black-box attacks based on composing speech and audio, without requiring white-box model access or optimized noise perturbations.

The benchmark covers overlapping speech, conversations involving multiple speakers, and mixtures of speech with non-speech sounds. Its questions refer implicitly to audio content, so the text prompt alone contains no explicit harmful information. This setup tests whether safeguards interpret the combined scene rather than relying solely on what is written in the prompt.

The reported attack success rate for Gemini 2.5 Pro is 66% despite enabled safety guardrails. The proposed SALMONN-Guard jointly examines speech, audio, and text, reducing the reported rate to 20%. These results show a substantial reduction while leaving successful attacks in the evaluation. They support inspecting the audio and its relationship to the text as part of multimodal safety judgments.
icml-2026-speech-audio-compositional-att.tldr: SACRED-Bench exposes safety failures in composed audio inputs, while SALMONN-Guard reduces reported attack success from 66% to 20%.

paragraphs: Hyperspectral image super-resolution needs to capture relationships across spatial locations and spectral information while controlling computation. Full attention is expensive, but restricting processing to windows weakens access to global relationships. SSDCN addresses this tradeoff through content-driven clustering that provides a compact basis for modeling structure across the image.

Its spatial-spectral dual-cluster block replaces point-to-point attention with learned low-rank structural bases, giving global modeling with O(KN) complexity. A progressive pyramid architecture then reuses the core tensor and spectral factors from coarser levels. Updating only the spatial factors reduces redundant reconstruction work as the model moves through the hierarchy.

A joint reconstruction loss supervises intermediate pyramid levels to maintain structural accuracy and prevent accumulated errors. Experiments report better quantitative metrics and visual quality than state-of-the-art methods while using substantially fewer parameters and floating-point operations. The gains combine a cheaper global modeling mechanism with reuse across reconstruction levels, addressing efficiency in both feature processing and progressive image reconstruction.
icml-2026-ssdcn-spatial-spectral-dual-cl.tldr: SSDCN combines spatial-spectral clustering and hierarchical feature reuse for more efficient, higher-quality hyperspectral super-resolution.

paragraphs: Offline black-box optimization seeks high-scoring new designs using only a fixed dataset. The central difficulty is judging designs outside the observed distribution. SPADE approaches this by using a diffusion model as a forward surrogate: it models the distribution of property scores conditioned on a design, rather than directly mapping a desired score back to a design.

Two additions adapt that predictive distribution for optimization. Calibrated Diffusion Estimation enforces consistency in statistical moments and pairwise rankings. Support-Proximity Regularization uses nearest-neighbor density estimation to incorporate proximity to the observed design distribution. These mechanisms connect predicted score behavior with information about where the dataset provides support.

The theoretical analysis shows that the regularizer is first-order equivalent to maximizing a Bayesian posterior with a valid design prior. This is a local equivalence claim, rather than an unrestricted identity. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance on Design-Bench tasks and a language-model data-mixture optimization benchmark, supporting the combination of expressive forward prediction and distribution-aware regularization.
icml-2026-support-proximity-augmented-di.tldr: SPADE combines diffusion-based score prediction with data-support regularization to improve offline design optimization.

paragraphs: A long agent task contains steps with different demands: some require strategic planning, while others involve routine execution. Fixed reasoning patterns spend effort uniformly or respond immediately throughout. CogRouter instead trains an agent to choose its cognitive depth at each step, using four levels inspired by ACT-R theory and ranging from instinctive responses to planning.

Training has two stages. Cognition-aware supervised fine-tuning establishes stable behavior for each cognitive level. Cognition-aware policy optimization then uses confidence-aware advantage reweighting to assign credit at the step level. The framework's guiding idea is that the appropriate reasoning depth should maximize confidence in the resulting action.

Experiments on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld report state-of-the-art performance with superior efficiency. These findings support adapting reasoning effort within a multi-turn task, where the computational needs can change from one action to the next. The contribution couples a defined hierarchy of reasoning behaviors with training that learns how to deploy those behaviors during interaction.
icml-2026-think-fast-and-slow-step-level.tldr: CogRouter trains agents to adapt reasoning depth at each step, improving reported task performance and efficiency.

paragraphs: Learning reasoning from several multimodal source models becomes difficult when their behavior changes over time. Those evolving reasoning distributions can pass systematic biases and drift into a target model. This paper frames multi-source alignment as a constraint satisfaction problem, using concept drift theory to organize how changing sources should influence training.

Autonomous Preference Optimization first bootstraps the target through supervised learning to bring it into the combined capability space of the sources. A second stage treats disagreements between models as dynamic negative constraints. Its multi-negative Plackett-Luce objective suppresses drifting reasoning trajectories while building a consistent shared representation of the source reasoning.

Experiments focus on chest X-ray interpretation. The authors report that their 7B model is more robust and exceeds even proprietary source models in average accuracy. They also introduce CXR-MAX, containing 170,982 reasoning trajectories from seven large multimodal models. The work supports using disagreement to constrain learning under drift, with its reported empirical evidence grounded in this chest X-ray setting.
icml-2026-turning-drift-into-constraint-.tldr: APO uses changing disagreements among source models as negative constraints to improve reasoning alignment under drift.

paragraphs: Zero-source hallucination detection must judge an answer using only its text and the original query. It has no access to model internals or external references. HCPD addresses this constrained setting by having a language-model agent break its judgment into several interpretable criteria, rather than relying on a single undifferentiated assessment.

The agent adaptively chooses a weighted set of criteria, scores the answer against each one, and combines those scores into a truthfulness measure. A reward-based alignment scheme teaches this adaptation using weak supervision derived only from semantic consistency. At inference, aggregating multiple samples aims to make decisions robust while retaining the criterion-level explanation.

The authors provide theoretical analysis supporting reliability and report consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in extensive experiments. The stated contribution is an explainable detector operating under the query–answer-only restriction. Its results support adaptive, multi-criterion judgment as a useful approach when reference-based verification is unavailable, with both the final score and the component assessments remaining interpretable.
icml-2026-zero-source-llm-hallucination-.tldr: HCPD detects hallucinations from query–answer text alone by combining adaptive, interpretable judgment criteria.
